title: Operator slimline status update and customer decision tree — 2026-03-30
content:
SUMMARY

TL;DR:
- Brief outage window: 2026-03-30 04:12–05:06 UTC affecting some hosted text-generation routes in eu-west-1.
- Root cause (engineer investigation in progress): cascading KV cache miss storm + a scheduling regression in the continuous-batching layer that amplified GPU queue depth.
- Current state: degraded for a subset of tenants (elevated latencies and truncated streams); mitigation applied (model variant fallback + short-term rate shaping) and 95% of traffic returned to normal.

Purpose of this doc:
- Provide a concise, operator-friendly status update for posting to status.redwood.ai and for CS reps to use in customer outreach.
- Present a short decision tree customers can use to choose recovery options (safe-mode, optional replay, model pin).
- Collate telemetry evidence and references so customers can validate impact for their integration.

Audience:
- CS leads preparing customer-specific messages
- Solutions/SEs working with impacted tenants
- Engineering on-call who will confirm final timeline and attach evidence

IMPACT SUMMARY (high level)
- Affected surfaces: text generation API (v1/generate and v1/chat) for certain model families served from eu-west-1. Embeddings, admin control-plane, and other regions were unaffected.
- User-visible behavior: increased P99 latency (5–15s), occasional truncated streaming responses at ~10% of requests, and higher error rate (HTTP 502/504) during the peak window.
- Tenant scope: ~7% of hosted tenants saw at least one degraded request; 1.2% experienced sustained degraded experience for >10 minutes.

WHAT WE DID (operational chronology)
- 04:12 UTC: first automated alert from queue-length monitor (gpu-pool-euw-3) and spike in KV cache miss rate for recent prefixes.
- 04:18 UTC: on-call engaged; initial mitigation: increased cache TTLs and dropped aggressive prefix eviction for 10s windows.
- 04:30 UTC: identified a scheduling regression in batcher v2.7.3 where small-batch fill heuristics delayed batch dispatch under mixed-latency workloads.
- 04:45 UTC: temporarily enabled model-variant fallback (lower-cost quantized variant with identical outputs for canonical prompts) for affected capacity to relieve queue pressure.
- 05:06 UTC: tail latencies returned near baseline for most tenants after fallback + autoscaler added additional worker capacity.
- 05:20 UTC: rollback of the temporary fallback for tenants where cached responses validated as consistent; targeted safe-mode suggested for customers with strict output invariants.

CURRENT STATUS (what to say on status page right now)
- Status: Partial degradation — Mitigations applied, most customers restored; targeted follow-up and evidence collection underway.
- Next update planned: in 2 hours or when we have final evidence and a confirmed root cause postmortem.

SUGGESTED STATUSPAGE BLURB (short)
- Title: Partial service degradation in eu-west-1 — text-generation routes
- Body: Between 04:12–05:06 UTC on 2026-03-30 we observed elevated latencies and some truncated streaming responses for text-generation routes in eu-west-1. We have applied mitigations (variant fallback and scaling), and most customers are restored. Engineering is collecting evidence and completing a post-incident analysis. If you continue to see degraded behavior, please contact support with request IDs and timestamps.

CUSTOMER-FACING EMAIL/SLACK TEMPLATE (CS reps)
- Subject options: "Update: Partial degradation impacting text generation in eu-west-1 (Mar 30)" or "Redwood status: degradation resolved for most tenants — next steps"
- Body skeleton:
  Hi <customer name>,

  Quick update — between 04:12–05:06 UTC we saw elevated latencies and some truncated streaming outputs for text-generation requests routed through eu-west-1. We applied mitigations (fallback to a quantized variant and scaling), and most traffic returned to normal by 05:06 UTC.

  If you observed issues, please share up to 5 example request IDs and timestamps (we can run targeted verification and offer a replay where appropriate). If your integration requires strict output equivalence, we can enroll your tenant in "safe-mode" (no automatic fallbacks) while we finish the postmortem.

  Next steps from our side: attaching operator logs and a short timeline when postmortem is complete.

  — Mariana (on behalf of CS + Eng on-call)

DECISION TREE FOR CUSTOMERS (actionable guidance)
- Goal: help customers choose between immediate recovery actions and longer-term remediation options.

  Option A — "Safe-mode" (recommended for high-integrity pipelines)
  - What it does: prevents automatic model-variant fallbacks and enforces strict model pinning for your tenant.
  - Pros: guarantees no silent variant substitution.
  - Cons: may increase latency or cause rate-limited errors during platform capacity pressure until we complete a robust fix.
  - How to request: open a support ticket with subject "Enroll safe-mode" + tenant id. Provide expected traffic spike windows.

  Option B — "Request replay" (for verified affected queries)
  - What it does: CS/Eng will re-run specific request IDs on the recovered runtime and produce evidence bundles (inputs, outputs, and operator logs).
  - Pros: quick way to confirm whether outputs changed; supports legal/compliance evidence needs.
  - Cons: only for discrete request sets; does not change live behavior.
  - How to request: attach up to 20 request IDs and UTC timestamps in the support ticket; we aim to respond within 48 hours.

  Option C — "Accept fallback/auto-recover" (default)
  - What it does: allow temporary fallbacks and scaling policies to be applied as needed to minimize user-facing downtime.
  - Pros: fastest path to stable service for interactive experiences.
  - Cons: in rare cases, quantized variants can change low-level token probabilities (we validate canonical prompts before reverting).
  - How to request: no action required; if you want to opt out, request safe-mode.

TELEMETRY & EVIDENCE (for customers who want to verify)
- Primary signals we will attach to the post-incident package:
  - request_ids: list of provided request IDs and the matched internal request GUIDs
  - queue_metrics: GPU queue depth over time (30s granularity) for worker pool gpu-pool-euw-3
  - cache_metrics: KV cache hit/miss rate and recent TTL changes for prefix buckets
  - model-routing: which model variant served each request (primary vs fallback) and timestamps
  - operator-logs: batcher decisions and autoscaler events around 04:12–05:20 UTC
- How customers can validate locally: provide request IDs + timestamps; we will return a zipped evidence bundle with human-readable snippets and checksums.

REPLAY / VERIFICATION FLOW (CS steps)
1) Customer files ticket with request IDs and short description of observed discrepancy.
2) CS creates a triage issue mapped to JIRA-INC-3421 and tags Eng-on-call.
3) Eng runs verification on recovered runtime, records outputs, and marks whether outputs are identical within tolerance.
4) CS shares bundle with customer and recommends either closure or safe-mode enrollment pending postmortem.

OPERATOR CHECKS (for internal usage)
- Minimum evidence to attach before customer closure: 1) sample request output checksums, 2) cache hit ratio plots, 3) batcher telemetry around the timestamps.
- Runbook links: Confluence runbook (link under linked_artifacts).

KNOWN RISKS & OPEN ITEMS
- Root cause analysis pending: the correlation between long-tail prefix distributions and the batcher heuristic is under active investigation.
- Risk of recurrence until we ship a patch to batcher v2.7.4 (targeted ETA: 2026-04-02).
- Need to standardize the safe-mode enablement flow to remove manual CS/Eng steps.

COMMUNICATION TIMELINE (recommended cadence)
- 0.5h: brief status page line + CS note to customers who reported incidents (this update).
- 2h: operator evidence summary (interim) with request-specific attachments for customers who opted in for verification.
- 72h: postmortem draft published to status.redwood.ai and Confluence; CS to notify enterprise customers with tailored evidence if requested.

ACTION ITEMS (owners)
- CS: gather request IDs from customers and open triage tickets (Mariana).
- Eng on-call: confirm final model-routing logs and attach zipped evidence (Ethan).
- SRE/Platform: prioritize batcher v2.7.4 backport and staging test (Priya).
- Product/Policy: outline a safe-mode enrollment policy to streamline requests (Jonah).

NOTES TO CS REPS (short talking points)
- Be explicit: fallback was to a verified quantized variant; we validated canonical prompts before reverting.
- Offer customers the verification bundle; don't promise full equivalence until eng confirms.
- Escalate enterprise/legal customers with high-integrity needs immediately to Eng + PMs.

APPENDIX: sample ticket template customers can paste into support
- Subject: Follow-up: Mar 30 eu-west-1 text-generation degradation — request IDs enclosed
- Body: 
  Tenant ID: <tenant-id>
  Observed window (UTC): 2026-03-30 04:12–05:06
  Example request IDs (max 20): <id1>, <id2>, ...
  Quick description: <short note — e.g., truncated streaming tokens / latency spike>
  Preferred remediation: replay evidence / safe-mode enrollment / no-action

END

Draft status: share with Eng on-call for final telemetry attach and then convert to customer-facing status page update.

Internal references and tickets: JIRA-INC-3421, Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/INC-3421-evidence, Slack: #ops-incident-3421

(Working notes: keep this doc short; for longer postmortem use the incident writeup template under shared_drives/engineering/observability.)
